title: Nested IF, IFS and SWITCH
explanation: IF chooses between **2** answers. Letter grades need more: A for 90+, B for 80+, C for 70+, and F below that. This lesson shows 3 ways to choose between several answers.

tasks.prompt: In D2, give Maya a letter grade by putting IFs inside each other: =IF(B2>=90, "A", IF(B2>=80, "B", IF(B2>=70, "C", "F"))). Then copy it down to D9.
tasks.teach: A **nested IF** puts another IF in the "if false" part. Excel checks the tests **in order** and stops at the first TRUE one, so start with the highest grade. Count your closing brackets: one per IF.
hints: Each new IF goes where the previous one's "if false" would go. You need 3 closing brackets at the end.
tasks.answer: =IF(B2>=90, "A", IF(B2>=80, "B", IF(B2>=70, "C", "F"))) in D2, then copy down to D9

tasks.prompt: Nested IFs get messy. In E2, do the same with IFS: =IFS(B2>=90, "A", B2>=80, "B", B2>=70, "C", TRUE, "F"). Then copy it down to E9.
tasks.teach: **IFS(test1, answer1, test2, answer2, ...)** lists test-and-answer pairs, checked in order. There's no "otherwise" part, so the last test is just **TRUE**, which always matches: it catches everything left over.
hints: Pairs of test, answer. End with TRUE, "F".
tasks.answer: =IFS(B2>=90, "A", B2>=80, "B", B2>=70, "C", TRUE, "F") in E2, then copy down to E9

tasks.prompt: Last one: the section codes M, A and E mean Morning, Afternoon and Evening. In F2, use SWITCH to turn the code into its name, then copy it down to F9.
tasks.teach: **SWITCH(value, match1, result1, match2, result2, ...)** compares one value against a list of exact matches. It's tidier than IFS when you're matching codes rather than ranges of numbers.
tasks.answer: =SWITCH(C2, "M", "Morning", "A", "Afternoon", "E", "Evening") in F2, then copy down to F9

recap: Nested IFs and IFS check tests in order and stop at the first TRUE, so start with the highest. IFS ends with TRUE as a catch-all. SWITCH matches exact values like codes.
